method.normalisation: comments and preprocessor lines removed; statements split at `;`/`{`/`}`; Ghidra temporaries (iVarN/uVarN/param_N/uStack_N/local_N/extraout_*/unaff_*/in_*) folded to V; every integer literal folded to N; whitespace removed. Two keys were computed per window: `callee_exact` (FUN_xxxxxxxx kept) and `shape` (FUN_xxxxxxxx folded to F).
method.ranking: clusters are ranked by DISTINCT FILE count, not by occurrence count: intra-function repetition is a loop, not an inline function. Windows of k = 1..6 statements were swept over 3318 canonical files / 112293 statements.

hard_rule: Semantics must be preserved exactly. Any change to a canonical recon/app/src or recon/net/src body must be re-proven with recon_kit.prove / net_recon_kit.prove AND tools/cfg_verify.py. The Unicorn differential harness is BLIND to dropped register/stack arguments, wrong indirection levels, stack writes, stack-buffer layout, wrong embedded constants and wrong loop strides -- 19 confirmed instances so far. Any change that touches argument passing or stack layout needs a disassembly-level review, not just a green harness run.

G7-B1.title: header extraction of identical static-inline definitions
G7-B1.why_first: no call site changes; a definition moved verbatim into a header cannot change codegen once the copies are proven byte-identical
G7-B1.gate: diff every copy before collapsing; compile-only + `nm` comparison of the affected objects; no recon_kit.prove needed if no function body changes

G7-B2.title: one declaration per logging entry point
G7-B2.why_second: it is a latent ABI defect, and every later batch that touches a log call would otherwise bake the wrong prototype in
G7-B2.gate: read each entry point's prologue in the disassembly to fix the true signature; then recon_kit.prove + cfg_verify on EVERY canonical file whose declaration changed (299+314+375+268 declarations across ~500 files)

G7-B3.title: assert and noreturn macros
G7-B3.gate: per-site argument-count check against the disassembly (the print and post halves do not pair 1:1); then recon_kit.prove + cfg_verify per file
G7-B3.depends_on: G6-B1 (the format/file/expr strings must be literals first)

G7-B4.title: log gate and irq-lock prologue
G7-B4.gate: disassembly review of the comparison sense (C06) and of the save/lock/ISB/restore quadruple (C07); then prove + cfg_verify

G7-B5.title: volatile accessor spelling normalisation, then macros
G7-B5.gate: two sub-passes: (a) normalise spellings of the SAME type only (unsigned/uint/unsigned int -> one spelling) -- textual, codegen-identical; (b) only then introduce G1_R*/G1_S* macros, per width, with a signedness audit of every consumer. Never merge int with unsigned int.

G7-B6.gate: read all 13 dispatch targets' prologues; disassembly-level review mandatory (dropped-argument class)

G7-B7.gate: one call at a time, by disassembly; no batching

clusters.title: Zephyr __ASSERT expansion (printk + assert_post_action pair)

proposed.form: macro (must stay a macro: __FILE__/__LINE__/#cond are only available at the expansion site, and a function would change the argument count)
proposed.app_signature: #define G1_ASSERT(cond) do { if (!(cond)) { printk("ASSERTION FAIL [%s] @ %s:%d\n", #cond, __FILE__, __LINE__); assert_post_action(); } } while (0)
proposed.net_signature: #define G1_NET_ASSERT(cond) do { if (!(cond)) { assert_print("ASSERTION FAIL [%s] @ %s:%d\n", #cond, __FILE__, __LINE__); assert_post_action(); } } while (0)
proposed.header: a NEW recon/headers/g1_assert.h (do not edit recon/symbols/*.h -- those are generated)
proposed.depends_on_G6: the three string operands are rodata pins today (rodata_99cbd = "ASSERTION FAIL [%s] @ %s:%d\n" alone has 1843 references across the trees). The macro is only writable once G6 batch B1 has turned them into literals.

clusters.risk: HIGH-VALUE / MEDIUM-RISK. The Unicorn differential harness is BLIND to dropped register/stack arguments, wrong indirection levels, stack writes, stack-buffer layout, wrong embedded constants and wrong loop strides -- 19 confirmed instances so far. Any change that touches argument passing or stack layout needs a disassembly-level review, not just a green harness run. Specifically: the shipped printk call passes 4 or 5 arguments depending on the site (937 app print-half sites vs 662 post-half sites; net 313 vs 268 -- the halves do NOT pair 1:1, so 275 app and 45 net print calls are NOT assert expansions and must not be swept into the macro). Collapsing a 5-argument site into a 4-argument macro silently drops a register argument and the harness will still pass. Per-site argument-count check against the disassembly is mandatory.

clusters.title: volatile-cast memory accessors (the single largest duplication in the corpus)

proposed.precedent: recon/net/src/FUN_01013650.c already defines and uses U8/U16/S16/U32/U64(p,o); it is the only file that does (4 #define sites, 1 file).

clusters.risk: HIGH-RISK DESPITE LOOKING MECHANICAL. Width and signedness are load-bearing: the reconstruction convention is that a global's access width and signedness must match the literal-pool value the original used (AGENTS.md methodology step 1). Mapping `*(volatile int*)` (977 sites) onto G1_R32 changes signed to unsigned and changes the C type of every comparison and shift that consumes it. `*(volatile unsigned*)`, `*(volatile uint*)` and `*(volatile unsigned int*)` are the same type spelled three ways and CAN be unified; `int` vs `unsigned int` cannot without checking every consumer. Do this as a spelling-normalisation pass first (variant -> canonical spelling of the SAME type), and only then introduce the macro. clusters.title: log-level gate: DEBUG_PRINT(...) else debug_print(...)
clusters.normalised_shape: if (*(volatile int*)N == N) { DEBUG_PRINT(N,N); } else { debug_print(N,N); }
clusters.cross_file_cluster_evidence: cluster_g7 k=6, `DEBUG_PRINT(N,N); } else { FUN_00019c70(N,N); } }` -- 42 distinct files, 56 occurrences; the k=4 prefix reaches 49 files.

proposed.form: macro (the two branches take the same literal, so a function would evaluate it twice / lose the compile-time gate)
proposed.signature: #define G1_LOG(gate, ...) do { if ((gate) == G1_LOG_GATE_VALUE) DEBUG_PRINT(__VA_ARGS__); else debug_print(__VA_ARGS__); } while (0)
proposed.prerequisite: the gate global and its compared value must be named first (it is a raw *(volatile int*)0x2000xxxx today) -- that is a G6-X/keep-symbolic RAM global, so the macro takes it as a parameter rather than baking it in.

clusters.risk: MEDIUM. Only ONE of the two branches is taken at runtime, so a swapped branch is invisible to any test that never flips the gate, and the parity harness seeds the gate global arbitrarily. Confirm the sense of the comparison per site from the disassembly.

clusters.title: irq_lock prologue: __set_BASEPRI_MAX(N); __ISB();
clusters.cross_file_cluster_evidence: cluster_g7 k=2 exact-callee: `__set_BASEPRI_MAX(N); __ISB();` -- 43 distinct files, 46 occurrences, both cores.

proposed.form: static inline function (no macro needed -- no token pasting, no __LINE__)
proposed.signature: static inline uint32_t g1_irq_lock(uint32_t prio) { uint32_t old = __get_BASEPRI(); __set_BASEPRI_MAX(prio); __ISB(); return old; }  static inline void g1_irq_unlock(uint32_t old) { __set_BASEPRI(old); }

clusters.risk: MEDIUM. Not every site saves and restores BASEPRI the same way, and some sites do the ISB and some do not. Only fold the sites whose full save/lock/ISB/restore quadruple matches; folding a save-less site into the saving inline ADDS a register read the original never made. That extra read is invisible to the harness (it compares non-stack writes, not reads).

clusters.title: net vtable-dispatch thunk
clusters.normalised_shape: void F(void){ uint32_t v = *(volatile uint32_t*)N; code fn = *(code*)(v + N); fn(); }
clusters.cross_file_cluster_evidence: cluster_g7 shape k=5, 13 distinct net files, 13 occurrences.

proposed.form: macro that generates the whole thunk body, because the two constants differ per site
proposed.signature: #define G1_NET_VTABLE_THUNK(name, obj_addr, slot) void name(void) { uint32_t v = *(volatile uint32_t *)(obj_addr); ((void (*)(void))(*(uintptr_t *)(v + (slot))))(); }

clusters.risk: MEDIUM-HIGH. `code fn` is a Ghidra pseudo-type; the real signature of the dispatched function is unknown and may take arguments in r0-r3 that the thunk passes through by accident of register state. Calling it as `void(*)(void)` is exactly the dropped-argument class the harness cannot see. Read each of the 13 targets' prologues before folding.

clusters.title: `((long long (*)(void))FUN_xxxx)()` call-through-cast idiom
clusters.concentration: 1012 occurrences but only 2 files -- this is intra-file repetition, not cross-file duplication, so its DEDUPE value is low. It is listed because the shape is a correctness hazard, not because collapsing it pays.

proposed.form: NOT a dedupe. Audit: replace each cast-call with a correctly prototyped extern declaration of the real callee.

clusters.risk: This is the harness-blind class in its purest form. Calling `device_info_text_width_get` through a `long long (*)(void)` cast makes the caller read r0:r1 as a 64-bit result when the callee only defines r0; on the hard-float ABI it also changes how a float return would be fetched. The harness compares the ABI return register(s) of the FUNCTION UNDER TEST, not of its stubbed callees, so it cannot see this. Fix by disassembly, one call at a time; do NOT batch.

clusters.title: conflicting extern declarations of the four logging entry points

proposed.form: one header with ONE declaration each, every per-file extern deleted
proposed.signature: recon/headers/g1_log.h: void DEBUG_PRINT(const char *fmt, ...); void debug_print(const char *fmt, ...); void log_message(const char *fmt, ...); void printk(const char *fmt, ...);   -- the concrete return type and variadic-ness must be READ OFF THE DISASSEMBLY of each entry point before this header is written, not chosen for tidiness.

clusters.risk: HIGHEST-PRIORITY DEFECT FOUND BY G7, and it is not really a dedupe -- it is a latent ABI bug. 37 files declare `void debug_print(void)` while 20 declare `void debug_print(int,...)`. On this build (-mfloat-abi=hard) a variadic function passes floating-point arguments in CORE registers while a non-variadic one passes them in FP registers, so the two declarations are not interchangeable. Each translation unit currently compiles against its own belief. Unifying them WILL change codegen in some files, so every affected canonical function must be re-proven.
